<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par150 />{{GHGmargin-letter|150|f}}
2. The rare cases in which a ''simple'' question is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} (as sometimes in Latin by ''an? is it?'') are really due to the suppression of the first member of a double question; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=13|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|g}}
(''b'') Disjunctive questions are, as a rule, introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} (''utrum—an?'') or sometimes by {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם}}<ref>{{GHGheb|text=וְאִם}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=24}} after a negative statement; we should, however, with Dyserinck read {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵין}}. Not less irregular is {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=אִם לֹא}} in the second clause of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=15}}, but the text can hardly be correct (cf. Moore, ''Judges'', New York, 1895, p. 337); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=11}} the second {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} introduces a fresh question which is only loosely connected with the first.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=28}} and in the third clause of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=13}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַאִם}} is best taken with Ewald in the sense of {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא}}, since {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} from its use in oaths (see above, {{GHGpar|149|b}}) may simply mean ''verily not''.</ref>—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=4}} (even with {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} repeated after {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם}} in a question which implies disbelief, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=17}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=8|hidebook=1}} f. special emphasis is given to the first member by {{GHGheb|text=הַאַף}} prop. ''is it even?'' The second member is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ|translate=or}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=36|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=1|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ הֲ}}), in each case before {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}, and hence no doubt for euphonic reasons, to avoid the combination {{GHGheb|text=אִם מ׳}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=19}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|h}}
Double questions with ({{GHGheb|text=וְאִם}}) {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} need not always be mutually exclusive; frequently the disjunctive form serves (especially in poetic parallelism; but cf. also e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=8}}) merely to repeat the same question in different words, and thus to express it more emphatically. So {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=17}} ''shall mortal man be just before God? or'' ({{GHGheb|text=אִם}}) ''shall a man be pure before his Maker?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=5}} f., 8:3, 10:4 f., 11:2, 7, 22:3, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=29}}. The second member may, therefore, just as well be connected by a simple {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=7|hidebook=1}} f., 38:16 f.22, 32, 39; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=5}} after {{GHGheb|text=מָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=17}} f. after {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּה}}; or even without a conjunction, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=4|hidebook=1}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|i}}
(''c'') With regard to ''indirect'' questions<ref>It should here be remarked that the distinction between direct and indirect questions cannot have been recognized by the Hebrew mind to the same extent as it is in Latin or English. In Hebrew there is no difference between the two kinds of sentence, either as regards mood (as in Latin) or in tense and position of the words (as in English). Cf. also {{GHGpar|137|c}}.</ref> after verbs of inquiring, doubting, examining,<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=6}} the {{GHGheb|text=הַ}} after {{GHGheb|text=לְהַגִּיד}} is explained from the fact that the latter, according to the context, implies ''to give information upon a question''.</ref> &c., simple questions of this kind take either {{GHGheb|text=הֲ|translate=whether}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=8}},<ref>Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=21}} we should read {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֹלָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֲיׄרֶ֫דֶת}} (''whether—whether'') instead of the article which is assumed by the Masora.</ref> or {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=7|verse=13}}; even before a noun-clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=1}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=10}} the indirect question is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}}, i.e. probably ''if perchance''. In disjunctives (''whether—or'') {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=18}} at the end (or {{GHGheb|text=אִם־לֹא}}—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=4}}), and {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}}—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=18}}, which is followed by {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}}; also {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}}—{{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=19}}. The formula {{GHGheb|text=מִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם}} has an affirmative force, ''who knows whether... not'', like the Latin ''nescio an'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=14}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|k}}
In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=7}}, 8 the relative pronouns {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ·}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} owing to the following {{GHGheb|text=לְמִי}} have become also interrogative, ''for whose cause?''

{{GHGmargin-letter|150|l}}
(''d'') {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} (cf. {{GHGpar|136|c}}) immediately after the interrogative serve to give vividness to the question; so also {{GHGheb|text=אֵפוֹא}} (for which {{GHGheb|text=אֵפוֹ}} five times in Job) ''then, now'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־אֵפוֹא הוּא|translate=who then is he?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַיֵּה אֵפוֹ}}<section end=par150 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
